title: The CSS Box Model - Margin, Padding and Border
summary: Explains the box model: every element is a rectangular box with content (width/height), padding, border and margin. Covers border shorthand, one-to-four value syntax, the div container and the Pesticide extension, then an exercise placing three boxes corner to corner.

concepts.heading: Every element is a box
points: Each HTML element is laid out as an invisible rectangle. height and width set the size of its content area; making a box taller pushes later elements further down the page.
width and height accept px or percentages. A width of 100% fills the parent's width.
From the inside out the layers are: content (width x height), padding, border, margin.

concepts.heading: border
points: Shorthand takes three values separated by spaces: thickness, style, colour. Example: border: 10px solid black.
Style can be solid, dashed and others; colour is any named or hex colour.
In this model the border sits outside the declared width/height. A bigger border does not shrink the content box; it adds to the element's overall size.

Fine-tune afterwards with border-width. It must come after the shorthand line, since later declarations override earlier ones. Example: border: 30px solid black; then border-top-width: 0 removes just the top.
border-width accepts one to four values (see multi-value syntax below).

concepts.heading: padding versus margin
points: padding is the gap between the content and the border, inside the border. The element's background colour covers the padding. Adding padding pushes the border outwards; the declared width/height stays the same.
margin is the gap outside the border, separating the element from its neighbours. Margin is transparent.
Two adjacent boxes each with margin 10px appear 20px apart in the lecture's example (10 from each side).
Padding adds space inside the visual box; margin adds space between boxes.
(Extra) Vertical margins between stacked block elements can collapse to the larger of the two instead of adding, so the 20px figure applies to the horizontal case.

concepts.heading: One to four values (padding, margin, border-width)
points: Four values go clockwise from the top: top, right, bottom, left.
Two values: first is top and bottom, second is left and right (e.g. 0 20px sets vertical 0, horizontal 20px).
One value applies to all four sides.
(Extra) Three values: top, left and right, bottom.
Single-side properties also exist: margin-left, padding-top, border-top-width and so on.

concepts.heading: Inspecting the box model
points: DevTools shows a nested diagram (margin, border, padding, content) with colours for each layer and the numbers editable.

Practice site: appbrewery.github.io/box-model/. Select an image, then in the Styles tab's box diagram type a margin of 100px to see gaps appear above/below, or padding of 100px to see space inside the border. Adding a 10px solid black border shows how padding sits inside it.

concepts.heading: The div element and Pesticide
points: div (content division) is a generic invisible container. Put any number of elements between its tags to group them so they can be styled or positioned together, e.g. an image with its caption.
A div has no look of its own, which is why it is taught only now that you can style boxes. It also adds structure to the HTML.
Pesticide is a free Chrome extension that outlines every element and div, making box model problems visible. Hold Ctrl and hover over a box to see its tag, classes and id in the bottom bar.

code_examples.caption: Border shorthand then override
Multi-value syntax
code_examples.code:
.a { margin: 10px; }                 /* all sides */
.b { margin: 10px 40px; }            /* top+bottom | left+right */
.c { margin: 0 10px 20px 30px; }     /* top | right | bottom | left */

task.name: 6.3 Box model: three boxes corner to corner
task.starting_point: index.html contains a list of TODO comments for you to follow like client instructions; goal.png shows the result, annotated with 20px padding, a 20px top/bottom and 10px left/right border on one box, and boxes touching corner to corner. The ref repo's index already holds the finished solution.
task.goal: Build three divs (ids first, second, third) of the same size, each with different padding, border and margin, so they touch diagonally at their corners.
steps: Add three divs to the body with ids first, second and third; put a paragraph of text in the first so padding is visible.
Give all divs height: 200px and width: 200px.
first: cadetblue background, padding 20px, border 10px solid black.
Reset the paragraph's margin to 0. Browsers give p a default margin of 1em top and bottom, which would push it off the div's edge.
second: gold background, solid black border with border-width of 20px top/bottom and 10px left/right (two-value form).
Work out the margin so second touches the bottom-right corner of first: first's outer width = 200 + 20 + 20 padding + 10 + 10 border = 260px, so margin-left: 260px.
third: indianred background, border 10px solid black, margin-left so its top-right corner meets second's bottom-left corner (second's left edge is at 260px and the box is 220px wide, giving 40px).
Check against the goal image; trial and error with DevTools works too.
task.expected_result: A staircase of three coloured boxes, each touching the next exactly at a corner with no gaps or overlap.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 06 - CSS Properties/06.03 - CSS Box Model/index.html

pitfalls: Forgetting the browser's default margin on p, which shifts text away from the div's padding.
Placing border-width before the border shorthand, which then overwrites it.
Forgetting that padding and border add to the rendered size when computing offsets (260px, not 200px).
Mixing up the order of four values: it is clockwise from top, not alphabetical.
Reference repo has an author footer element that is not in the exercise.

playground.coverage: Tasks and solution match the exercise (200px divs, three styled ids, margin-left 260 and 40). Two explore demos: a box-model dissector with sliders and box-sizing toggle, and a shorthand-values selector. Notes cover the four layers and margin 0 auto.
gaps_and_ideas: Starter already includes p { margin: 0 }; leave it out and add a task explaining why the paragraph looks off by default.
Add a task to write the three divs yourself, and one about wrapping an image plus caption in a div (the lecture's div section).
Add the arithmetic hint: 200 + 2x20 padding + 2x10 border = 260, to explain the margin values.
Add the order-matters demo: border then border-top-width, and swapped.
Add a Pesticide-style outline toggle in an explore demo (outline * { outline: 1px solid red }) to reveal invisible divs.
The box-sizing toggle is not in the lecture; label it as an extra.
